meta: Warm floor spot or hissing under the slab? We pinpoint and repair slab leaks in Oakley, CA with little digging. Clear price first. Call (888) 910-8644.
lead: Slab leak repair in Oakley, CA means fixing a water line that has failed in or beneath a concrete floor. We locate the break, explain your options and repair it with as little demolition as the job allows.
intro: A slab leak is a leak in a pressurized pipe that runs under or inside a concrete foundation slab. If your home is on a concrete slab, those lines are out of sight, so the first signs are usually a warm patch of floor, the sound of running water or a meter that will not stop.
This page covers the warning signs, what to do right away, how the break is found, your repair choices and what changes the price for homes in Contra Costa County.

sections.h2: There is a warm spot on my floor and I can hear water running
paras: A floor that feels warm underfoot, a faint hiss when the house is quiet or damp flooring with no obvious source often means a pressurized line is leaking beneath the concrete. Plumbers call this a slab leak, and it is a repair job rather than a mystery once the break is pinpointed.

sections.h2: Water is rising through the floor or the meter will not stop
paras: A leak under concrete can undermine flooring and soak cabinets quickly, so treat visible water as urgent. Our 24/7 emergency dispatch is available, and the steps below limit the damage while you wait.
do_now: Close the main shutoff valve at the house or at the meter box, then open a faucet to drain the lines.
Turn off the water heater, since a heater running on empty can be damaged. For a gas unit, set the control to pilot or off.
A gas smell alongside a floor problem means exit now, then 911 and PG&E at 1-800-743-5000, with the plumber after that.
Roll up rugs and lift cardboard boxes off the floor to keep wet material from spreading.
Photograph wet flooring, baseboards and the meter reading for your insurer.

sections.h2: Signs that point to a leak under the concrete
paras: No single sign proves it, but two or three together make a slab leak likely.

items.d: A hot water line leaking under the slab can warm the concrete in a small patch.
A hiss, trickle or rushing noise with every fixture closed.
The dial or low-flow indicator keeps turning with everything off.
Moisture wicks up walls and pushes laminate or wood out of shape.
Weak flow only on the hot side suggests the heater supply line.

sections.h2: Spot repair, reroute or repipe: choosing the right fix
paras: There are three standard ways to deal with a leaking slab line, and the right one depends on the pipe's condition, the number of leaks and your floors. Each trades cost and disruption differently.

sections.h2: How the break is found without breaking up the slab
paras: Finding the break comes first, and it is done with a meter test, acoustic listening and thermal imaging so the crew knows where to open the slab. The general methods are covered in our [[leak-detection|leak detection]] service, and slab work uses the same tools aimed at the floor.

Once the spot is marked, we cut only as much concrete as the repair needs, make the fix, pressure test the line and restore the opening. Whether a slab cut can be patched to match your flooring depends on what is on top, so ask us about tile, vinyl or hardwood before the work starts.

sections.h2: Water heaters and garages: common slab leak locations
paras: Hot lines often fail near the water heater, because heat and flexing are hardest on the pipe where it enters the floor. If the heater sits in a garage, a damp patch near its base can be a supply fitting leaking into the slab, not the tank itself.

Check the tank, the shutoff valve and the base for moisture before blaming the floor. If the tank is the problem, our [[water-heater-repair|water heater repair]] work covers it, and a leak beyond the heater's connections is the slab leak we handle here.

sections.h2: Meters, permits and what is yours to repair in Oakley
paras: Here in Oakley the District's pipe ends at the meter or backflow device, so a leak under your floor sits on your side. A slab leak sits on the owner's side, so the repair and cost are yours unless your insurance responds.

Whether a permit applies to a slab repair is a question for the City Building Division, and it should be answered before any concrete is cut. Neighbors in nearby [[plumber-brentwood-ca|Brentwood]] deal with a different water system, so check which utility serves your address first.

sections.h2: What drives the cost of a slab leak repair
paras: Slab jobs vary widely, so we give a clear price before work starts after the break is located.

factors.d: A break near a wall is simpler than one under the middle of a finished room.
Tile and hardwood take more careful removal and patching than bare concrete.
A spot repair, a reroute and a repipe differ greatly in materials and labor.
Several leaks on the same pipe often make a reroute the sensible choice.
Drying, flooring and drywall repairs are separate from the plumbing.

sections.insurance: Policies often cover sudden and accidental water damage but may exclude gradual leaks or the cost of accessing the pipe. Ask your insurer exactly what is covered, and keep photos and bills.
sections.call_line: Call (888) 910-8644 for a real number once we know where the leak is.

paras: After a repair, keep an eye on the meter for a few days and watch for new warm spots. If the home has had one slab leak, pipe condition becomes part of the conversation, and a plumber can tell you whether the rest of the line looks worn. Heavy water pressure is also hard on aging pipe, so ask for a pressure check while we are there.

faqs.q: How do I know if the leak is under my slab and not in a wall?
a: Warm floor patches, a hiss from the floor and a moving meter lean toward the slab. Damp drywall and a stain higher up usually mean a wall or ceiling line. A pressure test and listening gear tell us for sure.

faqs.q: Do you handle slab leak repair emergencies at night or on weekends in Oakley?
a: Yes, our 24/7 emergency dispatch covers active slab leaks. Shut off the main valve first, then call (888) 910-8644.

faqs.q: Will the repair damage my flooring?
a: Some opening is unavoidable, but we mark the smallest cut that works. How the patch looks depends on tile, vinyl or wood, so plan for flooring work afterward.

faqs.q: Is a whole-house repipe better than one repair?
a: It can be when pipes are old or multiple leaks appear. A single repair costs less up front, while a repipe reduces the chance of another break. Our plumber can show you the pipe's condition first.

faqs.q: Can the water stay on while you work?
a: The leaking line has to be isolated, and whether other fixtures keep running depends on how the pipes are laid out. Ask when you book so you know what to expect.

faqs.q: Is the pipe at the meter the district's responsibility?
a: Only the stretch ahead of the meter is the District's. A leak after that point is on the owner's side. The District can confirm the boundary for you.
